correctness.rationale: With the stated order of the free step and kick, Fourier evolution multiplies by exp(2ih cos(k+q_j)) after shifting the previous state to k+q_j. Iterating from the constant transform gives the suffix phasor S_n. The inverse transform gives J_m(2h|S_n|)^2; symmetry gives conditional mean zero, and Fourier derivative Parseval gives variance 2h^2|S_n|^2. Summing the phasor correlations r^|j−k| yields exactly the finite-time variance including the negative transient. The forward phasor martingale differences have squared norm conditional mean 1−r² and pseudovariance (r^4−r²)U_(j−1)^2. The positive wrapped-Gaussian density makes the circle walk uniformly ergodic, so the average pseudovariance vanishes and the real covariance limit is isotropic. The telescope divides the limit by 1−r, giving variance alpha/2 in each coordinate. The reversal is only used in distribution; equivalently the radius equals that of the forward sum from U_0 to U_(n−1), pathwise. Rayleigh radius and exponential normalized variance follow. For any deterministic radii s_n→s, the characteristic functions J_0(4h sqrt(n) s_n sin(k/(2 sqrt(n)))) tend to J_0(2hsk), so the corresponding measures converge weakly (including s=0). Applying this to any Skorokhod coupling of the convergent random radii proves convergence in distribution of the conditional measures. A uniform angle independent of the Rayleigh radius yields the first coordinate of a circular Gaussian, proving the claimed annealed variance 2h² alpha. Bounded differences give uniform scaled higher moments, justifying the reported variance-fluctuation moment limit.
residual_risks: The FFT and Monte Carlo checks are finite approximations only. The proof concerns fixed finite noise, a delta-site launch on the infinite lattice, and weak convergence in distribution of measures, not almost-sure convergence along one history.

value.rationale: A single diffusive width or an ensemble Gaussian could suggest an individual run has a similar cloud. The result gives instead an order-one distribution of widths and the exact shape of a conditional profile on the same spatial scale, and explains how their mixture produces a Gaussian. These are quantitatively useful for deciding whether averaging over histories is essential in this model, rather than an additional fit of the known variance slope.
residual_risks: No value claim is based on empirical finite-ring simulations or extrapolation to other initial states or noise laws.
